key_insight: Co2In balances plasticity and stability in incremental learning by separating fast knowledge acquisition in working memory from persistent retention in long-term memory.
engineering_relevance: For computational science and engineering workflows that require continual model updates, Co2In offers a memory-efficient strategy to incorporate new information without catastrophic forgetting.
method: Working memory learns from new data and encodes knowledge into parameters.
A consolidation step extracts underlying patterns and compresses them into a compact knowledge representation.
The knowledge representation and patterns are integrated as separate layers into long-term memory.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet under exemplar-free Class-IL and Task-IL settings, where it achieved state-of-the-art performance with efficient memory use.
watch_item: The approach relies on a consolidation and integration pipeline that may add implementation complexity and could be sensitive to how knowledge representations are extracted and merged.
paper_title: Co2In: a Bi-level Memory Incremental Learning Framework with Knowledge Encoding, Consolidation, and Integration
